topic: USS Abraham Lincoln's record-length deployment and reported crew welfare crisis
summary: The USS Abraham Lincoln, deployed to the Middle East since November 21, 2025 amid the Iran war, spent over 250 days at sea -- including more than 200 consecutive days without a port call, the longest continuous carrier deployment in the modern U.S. Navy. Multiple outlets reported a crew mental-health crisis severe enough that sailors attempted to go overboard, alongside food and water shortages and broken plumbing/sanitation. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth publicly called the reports 'completely misrepresented'; President Trump said the carrier had not been deployed 'nearly long enough.' Thirteen Senate Democrats, including the full Senate Armed Services Committee minority, sent Hegseth a formal letter demanding answers and a bipartisan congressional delegation visit. The Lincoln was relieved by the USS George Washington and began its return to San Diego around August 20, 2026.
